title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 9-11). Grothendieck works with ½-simplicial (semi-simplicial: face maps only) complexes L. of modules over a ring k. He has a class of 'special' objects, and stronger notions 'très spécial' and 'strictement spécial'. The structure theorem is Prop. 1 with its corollaries, on earlier pages. It says a special L. is, up to isomorphism, a finite direct sum of standard pieces Λ^i 𝓛. ⊗ M_i (i ≥ 1) and Λ^j Ψ. ⊗ N_j (j ≥ 0). Here 𝓛. is the standard ½-simplicial module of rank n+1 in degree n (free on the vertices of Δ^n). Ψ. is the companion of rank n in degree n. The M_i, N_j are coefficient modules, and the N_j compute the homology: rg 𝓗_j = ν_j. Proposition 2, stated on p.9, says special (resp. très spécial) objects are stable under ⊗ and under the tensor operations Λ^i (and perhaps Γ^i, Sym^i).

This page, part 1 (end of the ⊗ case). Define the rank function ρ(n) = rg_k L_n = Σ_{1≤i≤n+1} μ_i C(n+1,i) + Σ_{0≤j≤n} ν_j C(n,j), with μ_i = rg M_i and ν_j = rg N_j. Each term C(n+1,i), resp. C(n,j), is a polynomial of degree i, resp. j, in n. So if some μ_i or ν_j is nonzero, ρ(n) is bounded below, for large n, by a polynomial of degree i, resp. j.

Consequence. The tensor product of two finite-type special objects has rank function equal to the product of two polynomials, hence of bounded polynomial degree. Its components are free of finite type, and by Künneth/Eilenberg-Zilber its homology is too. So only finitely many M_i, N_j can be nonzero. This is exactly the finiteness condition still missing on p.9 to conclude that the tensor products are special.

This page, part 2 (start of the case of the exterior power Λ^k). The superscript k means the k-th exterior power, a notational clash with the base ring k.
- The formula for Λ^k of a direct sum, together with case 1°, reduces the problem to Λ^k of a single block Λ^i 𝓛. ⊗ M or Λ^j Ψ. ⊗ N.
- The circled, partly crossed-out passage writes L. as a direct factor of something of the form Λ𝓛 ⊗ P ⊕ ΛΨ ⊗ P' and refers back to Cor. 1 and Cor. 2. It also invokes Λ^k of a sum once more.
- One may assume M, N free ('OPS' = on peut supposer), and then M = k, N = k.
- Hence one is reduced, as continued on p.11, to showing that Λ^k(Λ^h Ψ_{±}) and similar objects are special. That is done using freeness of the components and the homotopy triviality of one of the blocks.

On the next page this rank bookkeeping becomes a classification remark: a très spécial L. is determined up to isomorphism by the function n ↦ rg L_n and the homology ranks ν_j. The proof uses that the binomial polynomials C(n,i) form a Z-basis of integer-valued polynomials.

Purpose. These are finiteness and stability lemmas in a dévissage of ∂-perfect ½-simplicial complexes, aimed at multiplicative structures (λ-operations) on such complexes.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. 'Bounded below by a polynomial of degree i' is correct, since all coefficients are nonnegative.
Notational clash: the superscript k in Λ^k (exterior power) is the same letter as the base ring k.
The circled middle passage is heavily crossed out and its exact logic (direct factor of Λ𝓛⊗P ⊕ ΛΨ⊗P', with appeal to Cor. 1 and Cor. 2) cannot be fully reconstructed.

ideas.what: Rank function of a special ½-simplicial module as a nonnegative combination of binomials C(n+1,i), C(n,j); used to force finiteness of the decomposition under tensor product
ideas.modern_name: Polynomial growth / Hilbert-function-type argument for functors on the semi-simplex category (Δ_inj); binomial expansion of dimension functions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Similar polynomiality phenomena appear in FI-module theory (Church-Ellenberg-Farb, 2012) and in Dold-Puppe style analyses; nothing specific for this lemma

ideas.what: Reduction of the stability of 'special' complexes under exterior powers to elementary blocks, via Λ^k of a direct sum and reduction to free coefficients
ideas.modern_name: Dévissage for non-additive (polynomial) functors applied to semi-simplicial modules; λ-structure on a category of perfect complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold-Puppe (1961) for non-additive functors on simplicial modules; the λ-ring formalism goes back to SGA 6 (Berthelot, Grothendieck, Illusie)
ideas.where_published: SGA 6 treats λ-structures on K-groups, but not this semi-simplicial dévissage

missed.claim: The classification of special ½-simplicial modules by standard blocks Λ^i𝓛 ⊗ M_i, Λ^jΨ ⊗ N_j, with rank functions expanded in the binomial basis, anticipates the representation-stability / FI-module picture. There, dimension functions of finitely generated objects over injection categories are eventually polynomial and are expanded in binomials. It is a mild, unexploited link between Grothendieck's semi-simplicial dévissage and later work on functors on Δ_inj/FI.
missed.quote: ρ(n) = rg_k L_n = Σ μ_i (n+1 choose i) + Σ ν_j (n choose j) … minoré par un polynôme de degré i resp j
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest only. The argument itself is elementary, but it shows Grothendieck using binomial-basis rank bookkeeping for semi-simplicial objects decades before the FI-module literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine finiteness step (rank counting with binomials) inside an unpublished dévissage. The surrounding program of λ-structures on ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes is itself little known, but this page holds no striking new result.
transcription_corrections: '[?] tend [?] vers ∞ [?] et minoré [?]' likely reads 'ρ(n) tend vers ∞ et est minoré par un polynôme de degré i resp. j'.
'OPS' = 'On peut supposer'; the line likely says one may suppose M, N free (or reduce to that case), hence M = k (resp. N = k), using the formula for Λ^k of a sum.
'Λ𝓛. ⊗ M ou Λ𝓛. ⊗ N' should probably read Λ^i𝓛. ⊗ M (or similar) and Λ^jΨ. ⊗ N, the two block types of the structure theorem.

The circled passage seems to read 'D'où L. est facteur direct de L'. = Λ𝓛 ⊗ P ⊕ ΛΨ ⊗ P' …' with references to 'cor. 1 et cor. 2'; the transcribed '$D_\cdot$' is probably 'D'où' rather than a complex D.
Under the sums: 'pol. de degré i en n' and 'pol. de degré j en n'.
